coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 10 units (the domain directory itself plus 9 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md), 58 .md files. Matches the expected 10 units / 58 files exactly. Every file was read in full through the 3a implementer-simulation / 3b rubric / 3c devil's-advocate cycle. Rubric dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for every unit in this domain: personas are referenced not redefined ('Personas from meta/personas.md - referenced, never redefined', ticketing-box-office-index.md:53), the problem statement and constraints live in meta/, and there is no competitive content in a feature sub-tree. Dimensions 3, 7 and 8 are scored for all 10 units. This is an exceptionally strong sub-tree: decision logs, Deep Think annotations with rejected hypotheses, exhaustive edge-case tables and role lenses are present in every leaf. The findings below are concentrated in (a) two cross-feature contradictions that make an inventory rule and a money obligation unsatisfiable, and (b) a large class of stale cross-references and stale deferral markers left behind by completed pipeline stages.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether creating a guest-list allocation reserves matching inventory in the manifest (a hold) or is merely a right to name guests that competes with public sale. Nothing in the tree states the coupling rule, and the two candidate answers produce different manifest writes on every comp issuance (held-1/comp+1 versus remaining-1/comp+1) and opposite outcomes on a sold-out show.
findings.claim: 19.01.02 states normatively that the artist hold IS the guest-list inventory (so comp units are reserved and untouchable by public sale), while 19.03.01/19.03.02/19.03.03 state normatively that an allocation reserves nothing, loses a race for the last unit to a paid sale, and is worthless on a sold-out room. Both are unmarked. They cannot both hold: a hold is by construction net out of `remaining`, so a public sale cannot reach it, yet 'paid sale wins' is presented as the general rule.
findings.evidence: 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:20 (Role Lens, Musician) — "Owns and manages their **artist hold** — the block reserved for their guests, their team and their own comps, and the block 19.03 draws the guest list from."; :64 (default deadlines) — "Artist hold bound to a guest-list allocation | The guest-list close (owned by `19.03.01`) | The hold *is* the guest-list budget; releasing it earlier strands the artist's guests"; :194 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "The artist hold **is** the inventory the guest list draws from". CONTRADICTED BY 19.03.01-guest-list-allocation-submission.md:58 — "Race: comp issuance vs a public sale for the last unit | Allocation is valid but the manifest is empty at issuance. Paid sale wins by default (it is money); the promised allocation is undeliverable"; :74 — "Show sold out; party has unspent allocation | The allocation is real but the inventory is gone — the party holds a right they cannot exercise"; 19.03.02-comp-issuance-manifest-impact.md:60 — "Comp issued with no inventory left | Issuance fails atomically; allocation not spent. The allocation was a right to name guests, not a right to conjure seats"; :141 D-09 — "on losing a race for the last unit the paid sale wins and the comp fails"; 19.03.03-door-time-guest-list-changes.md:47 — "Room is sold out; guest at the door | No inventory, so no comp is possible regardless of allocation"; 19.03-guest-list-comps-cx.md:31 — "A party with 20 comps and a sold-out room has 20 comps they cannot use". 19.03.01's Happy Path step 1 (:43) creates an allocation with no hold at all: "the Operator creates the artist allocation on the show, funder = artist, quantity = 20 units".

findings.forcedInvention: How the cancellation refund obligation is created and discharged for a walk-up ticket sold for cash to an anonymous buyer with no contact channel and no reversible payment instrument. The implementer must invent the obligation record's contents, the discharge rule, and whether such a cancellation can ever reach Discharged.
findings.claim: 19.05.04 explicitly permits a completed walk-up sale with zero buyer identity and zero contact channel; 19.06.02's cancellation model requires every paid ticket to become a named, tracked obligation refunded to the original payment method, with the fan proactively contacted when that method fails, and forbids the cancellation from completing while any obligation is undischarged. For a cash walk-up on a show cancelled between doors and stage time (a scenario 19.06.02 itself names — 'the singer lost their voice, the venue flooded'), these rules are jointly unsatisfiable and no text reconciles them.
findings.evidence: 19.05.04-walk-up-day-of-show-sales.md:124 D-06 — "Every walk-up sale produces a ticket record that is itself the proof of purchase; a delivery channel is offered but optional, and **no buyer contact is required to complete a cash sale**"; :21 (Fan Role Lens) — "No account, no contact details, and no barcode are required to complete a cash sale (D-06)"; :61 — "an anonymous cash walk-up is valid and completes without capturing any buyer detail". AGAINST 19.06.02-event-cancellation-mass-refund.md:112 D-07 — "Refunds return only to the buyer's original payment method; a dead method escalates to a tracked, contacted alternative-payout incident, never a silent keep"; :107 D-02 — "A cancellation is not complete while any refund is undischarged"; :47 — "Six named incidents (name + amount + ticket) held open until discharged; the cancellation cannot reach Discharged while any remain"; :48 — "The fan is proactively contacted for an alternative destination — never told 'your card expired, therefore we keep your money', which is a forbidden terminal state (D-07)". 19.06.02's only post-close guard is :49 ("Cancelled after the box office closed ... `409 CANCEL_AFTER_CLOSE`"), which does not cover the doors-open-to-close window in which walk-up sells.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether a show's age restriction is inherited from a domain-16 room record (Operator confirms or raises a default) or is declared from scratch by the Operator per show with no upstream source. The two produce different configuration flows and a different empty state.
findings.claim: 19.04.04's Behavior, Happy Path and Cross-Cut Notes all assert normatively that the age restriction originates in the room's licence in domain 16, while the same file's Q-04 records as RESOLVED that domain 16 carries no audience age restriction at all and that the restriction is Operator-declared per show. The body text was never corrected, so Happy Path step 1 reads a field that the file itself establishes does not exist.
findings.evidence: 19.04.04-door-age-id-verification.md:27 (Behavior) — "A show carries an age restriction **sourced from the room's licence (domain 16)** and adjustable upward by the Operator for a specific show."; :35 (Happy Path 1) — "Room's licence (domain 16) supplies the default age restriction; Operator confirms or raises it for this show."; :93 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "Touches **16 Venues, Studios & Spaces** — the restriction originates in the room's licence, which is a room record." CONTRADICTED BY the same file :115 Q-04 — "~~Does domain 16 model the room's licensed age restriction structurally, or is it free text?~~ **RESOLVED — neither: 16 carries no audience age restriction at all.** ... There is therefore **no upstream default to inherit, and the restriction is Operator-declared per show here**." Corroborated at ticketing-box-office-index.md:110 Q-12 — "(3) **Licensed age restriction** — **no**: D-72's US profile locks exactly five statutory slots ... and an age restriction is not among them, so `19.04.04` Q-04's requirement currently lands on nobody."

findings.forcedInvention: The denominator of the held-inventory alert threshold, and the value of `remaining` at manifest initialisation. `sellable` is given two incompatible definitions across the two files that jointly own the counter model, and the alert fires at different points under each.
findings.claim: 19.01.02 defines sellable inventory as `capacity - killed` and expresses the held-inventory alert as `remaining <= max(10% of sellable, 20 units)`. 19.05.01 states `remaining = sellable` at initialisation, which is only true when `held = 0`; its own Happy Path gives the initialisation as `remaining = capacity - killed - held`. On a 300-cap room with a 40-unit hold the two readings put the alert threshold at 30 versus 26 and make the Initialised state display a number that is wrong by the held quantity.
findings.evidence: 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:96 (Happy Path 2) — "System instantiates the manifest and **derives sellable inventory as `capacity − killed`**"; :87 — "`remaining ≤ max(10% of sellable, 20 units)` **and** `held > 0` | Alert fires to the Operator"; :157 (Constrained state) — "`remaining ≤ max(10% of sellable, 20)` while `held > 0`". AGAINST 19.05.01-live-count-manifest-state.md:43 (Happy Path 1) — "counters initialise from it — **`remaining = capacity − killed − held`**"; :77 (Initialised state) — "All activity counters at their starting values; **`remaining = sellable`**"; :62 (Empty edge case) — "Initialised state: all activity counters at zero, **`remaining = sellable`**". The domain cross-cut file compounds it by using `sellable` for the decrementing count: ticketing-box-office-cx.md:60 — "decrementing the manifest's sellable count and incrementing comp"; :68 — "Issuance writes sellable−1 / comp+1 in one transaction" (an operation that changes neither `capacity` nor `killed`, so it cannot decrement `sellable` under 19.01.02's definition).

findings.forcedInvention: The amortisation denominator for a per-order mandatory fee inside the per-tier headline all-in price. At browse time the order size is unknown, so `all_in(tier)` is not computable, and the implementer must invent an assumed basket size (1? 2? cart quantity?).
findings.claim: 19.01.03's headline price formula adds 'amortised per-order mandatory fees' to a per-tier figure, while D-02 makes that same headline the exact total charged, captured once and never re-derived. No text supplies the amortisation basis, and D-05/DT-05 simultaneously forbid amortising per-order fees into per-ticket lines. Two implementers would produce different headline prices for the same show, and a fan whose basket size differs from the assumed one would be charged a per-ticket figure different from the one first shown — which the file itself classifies as a P1 compliance incident.
findings.evidence: 19.01.03-fee-structure-all-in-pricing.md:34-37 — "all_in(tier) = face_value + Σ(per-ticket mandatory fees, each rounded at its own line) + **amortised per-order mandatory fees**        [see per-order handling below] + tax(...)"; :42 (the display/charge invariant) — "The all-in total shown to a Fan at first impression is the **exact total charged** — the same number at browse, cart and charge... any observed divergence is a P1 compliance incident routed to 24"; :116 D-05 — "Per-order fees remain order-scoped for settlement and refunds, **never amortised into per-ticket lines**"; :92 DT-05 — "amortising a per-order fee into per-ticket lines corrupts settlement... Per-order fees are disclosed at order level in the headline math but remain a distinct order-scoped line". The tracked question at :125 Q-01 covers only whether mandatory fees sit *in* the headline versus *alongside* it, never the basis on which they would be divided.

findings.claim: 19.01.04 asserts in its Behavior and Cross-Cut Notes that seat maps are a domain-16 room asset, while its own Q-01 records that assertion as wrong and tracks the ownership collision onward. The normative body text was left uncorrected, so an implementer reading the Behavior section builds seat-map storage against a domain that has declined to carry it.
findings.evidence: 19.01.04-seating-model-ga-reserved-seat-maps.md:31 (Behavior) — "**Seat maps are a room asset (domain 16) reused across shows**; the show selects a *configuration* of the room, and the manifest is instantiated from it."; :76 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "seat maps and per-configuration licensed capacity are room assets owned there". CONTRADICTED BY the same file :94 Q-01 — "**Collision recorded, not resolved**: the same DT-04 declines seat identities and map geometry — *\"The room does **not** carry **seat identities or map geometry** ... Both domains are pointing at each other\"* — so **this file's assertion that *\"seat maps are a room asset (domain 16)\"* is wrong**, and the reconciliation is tracked as `16.01.02` Q-02."
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer follows Behavior line 31 and models seat identities/geometry as read-only reads from a domain-16 room record. Domain 16 (16.01.02 DT-04/D-05) does not store them, so reserved and mixed shows have no seat identities to instantiate the manifest from and 19.01.04 Happy Path step 2 ('system instantiates the manifest at the right granularity') cannot run.

findings.claim: 19.05.05 authors the counter-attestation outcome set as three distinct values — counter-attested, declined, lapsed — and states the rule 'never collapsing silence into consent'. 19.07.04 names the same lapse outcome `Accepted (lapsed)`, embedding 'Accepted' in the state that the authoring file insists is not acceptance. The enum a downstream consumer builds differs depending on which file it reads, and any settlement gate written as a prefix or membership test on 'Accepted' would treat silence as consent — the exact outcome both files forbid.
findings.evidence: 19.05.05-box-office-close-certified-statement.md:121 D-07 — "The statement records three distinct outcomes — **counter-attested, declined, and lapsed** — never collapsing silence into consent"; :83 (States) — "**Counter-attestation lapsed** | Deadline passed with no response | Recorded on the statement as lapsed — silence as silence, not consent". AGAINST 19.07.04-manual-count-entry-attestation.md:124 D-08 — "a lapse is recorded as **Accepted (lapsed)** — never as an active acceptance"; :85 (States) — "**Accepted (lapsed)** | Response window expired with no Musician action | Distinct from an active acceptance"; :58 — "On lapse → `Accepted (lapsed)`, a state **textually distinct** from an active acceptance". The consequence is live rather than cosmetic: 19.07.04:132 Q-01 leaves open "whether a lapsed window blocks settlement or permits it", so the state name already presumes the answer the question has not taken.
findings.failure_scenario: A settlement gate implemented from 19.07.04 tests `status.startsWith('Accepted')` (or an enum grouping Accepted-family values) and releases payout on a statement the artist never saw, while the same gate implemented from 19.05.05's three-value set blocks it. Same show, two implementations, opposite money outcomes.

Every child is marked `[SURFACE]` and captioned as a breadth pass, while 9 of the 12 children now carry `[DEEP]` or `[PARTIAL]` in their own headers; and the index states counts for the CX file that are roughly two-thirds of the actual content.

findings.claim: 19.01.05 routes the only zero-cost path to an accessible ticket to sub-domain '19.02' in three places. 19.02 is On-Sale, Announce & Presale Access; comps and guest list are 19.03. The domain cross-cut file states the same rule correctly against 19.03, so the two disagree with no marker.
findings.evidence: 19.01.05-accessible-seating-companion-tickets.md:21 (Fan Role Lens) — "Operator rights grant no self-comp path into accessible inventory (**comps route through 19.02**, never through this purchase flow)"; :61 (edge case) — "no Operator self-comp path exists here (**comps are 19.02**)"; :97 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "Touches **19.02 Comps & Guest Lists** — the only path to a zero-cost accessible ticket is a comp issued in **19.02**". findings.claim: 19.01.03 names sub-domain 19.03 as the owner of on-sale/checkout and of the door-sale transaction surface. 19.03 is Guest List & Comps; checkout is 19.02.04 and walk-up is 19.05.04. The mis-numbering is the exact transposition of finding #009 and appears in a Cross-Cut Note, which is the edge a downstream stage follows.
findings.evidence: 19.01.03-fee-structure-all-in-pricing.md:104 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "Touches **19.03 On-sale / Checkout** and **19.05 Box Office (walk-up)** — the walk-up fee profile defined here is consumed by the door-sale surface; this feature owns the profile, those own the transaction."; :67 (edge case) — "The door-sale transaction surface itself lives in **19.03/19.05**; this feature owns only the *fee profile* it consumes." Against the domain index Children table (ticketing-box-office-index.md:34-35), where 19.02 is 'On-Sale, Announce & Presale Access' and 19.03 is 'Guest List & Comps', and against 19.05.04-walk-up-day-of-show-sales.md:105, which correctly names 19.01.03 as the fee-profile source consumed by the window.
findings.failure_scenario: The walk-up fee profile's consumer edge is drawn from 19.01.03 to Guest List & Comps rather than to the checkout (19.02.04) and window (19.05.04) surfaces, so the fee-disclosure obligation D-08 places on the door sale ('the buyer must never face an undisclosed door premium') is not wired to any surface that takes payment.

findings.claim: 19.02.05 names two different recipients for the same early-hold-release prompt, both citing D-05. The decision itself says the prompt goes to the Operator; the Cross-Cut Note says it goes to the hold owner. On an artist hold these are different people with different permissions, so the notification target is undetermined.
findings.evidence: 19.02.05-sold-out-waitlist-demand-capture.md:110 D-05 — "Waitlist depth surfaces an early-hold-release *prompt* to **the Operator**, never an automatic release"; :88 DT-03 — "the **Operator's demand panel** surfaces a 'release N held tickets to the waitlist?' CTA... never overrides the holder's control of their own allocation". AGAINST the same file :95 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "waitlist depth is the signal that surfaces an *early-release prompt* to **the hold owner** (D-05). The trigger direction is 19.02.05 → 19.01.02: this feature reads hold-pool size and emits a release CTA". The distinction is live because 19.01.02:20 gives the Musician ownership of the artist hold while 19.01.02:22 makes the Operator "the only role that can act on another party's hold".
findings.failure_scenario: The release CTA is built into the Musician's surface (per the Cross-Cut Note) on a show where the hold is a venue or promoter hold they cannot act on, or built Operator-only (per D-05) so the artist never learns their own unspent allocation is the thing standing between a waitlist and a sale.

findings.failure_scenario: A remediation pass resolving the D-12 licence-lapse trigger follows the Q-05 citation, reads an unresolved [OWNER] question about deal-scoped hold visibility, and either reports the licence-validity dependency as still blocked (it is discharged by 16.02.01 D-06/D-10/D-11/D-14) or conflates the two into one owner decision.

findings.claim: 19.07.04's hard-block integrity check cites sub-domain 19.06 as the source of licensed capacity. 19.06 is Refunds, Cancellations & Rescheduling and holds no capacity figure; licensed capacity is read-only from domain 16 via 19.01.02 D-03. The check is the only hard block on the manual-entry path, so its input source being mis-named matters.
findings.evidence: 19.07.04-manual-count-entry-attestation.md:37 — "| Capacity ceiling | `paid + comp ≤ licensed capacity` **(19.06)** | **Hard block** — cannot attest until corrected or capacity is confirmed overridden with a reason; you cannot legally admit more than capacity |". AGAINST 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:211 D-03 — "Licensed capacity is **read-only here, sourced from domain 16's room configuration**", and 19.01.02:29 — "Licensed capacity is a hard ceiling supplied by the **room configuration** in domain 16 (per-configuration, not per-room — `19.01.04 DT-02`)". The domain index Children table (ticketing-box-office-index.md:37) names 19.06 as 'Refunds, Cancellations & Rescheduling'.
findings.failure_scenario: The manual-entry capacity hard block is wired to a refunds-domain figure that does not exist, so the only structural guard against an attested count exceeding the room's legal occupancy either fails to resolve or is silently skipped — and 19.07.04 D-06 makes this check the sole hard gate before an attestation becomes immutable and feeds settlement.
